sources.entry: StackStorm - StackStorm (aka _IFTTT for Ops_) is event-driven automation for auto-remediation, security responses, troubleshooting, deployments, and more. Includes rules engine, workflow, 160 integration packs with 6000+ actions and ChatOps. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python

summary.one_liner: StackStorm is an event-driven automation platform that connects existing tools and services and runs actions, rules, and workflows in response to events ("IFTTT for Ops").
summary.what_it_does: StackStorm uses sensors to watch external systems and fire triggers when events occur, and rules to map those triggers to actions or workflows. Workflows chain multiple actions together with ordering, transition conditions, and data passed between steps. Actions can be Python plugins or any script, made available by adding metadata, and can be run manually via CLI, API, or web UI. Automations are grouped into packs for distribution and sharing, and content is stored as code. The audit trail records execution history and can be forwarded to external logging tools such as LogStash, Splunk, statsd, or syslog. The platform is made of loosely coupled microservices communicating over a message bus, and it exposes a REST API, CLI client, web UI, and Python client bindings.
how_to_run: Get a clean 64-bit Linux machine that meets the system requirements
Run the installer script: curl -sSL <url> | bash -s -- --user=st2admin --password=<password>
Read the documentation for installation and authoring guides
notable: Rules engine mapping triggers to actions or workflows with payload matching
Workflows that combine actions into multi-step automations with conditional transitions
Packs bundle integrations and automations; shared via the StackStorm Exchange
Actions can be any script, registered by adding a few lines of metadata
Audit trail of executions with forwarding to Splunk, LogStash, statsd, or syslog
caveats: Requires a clean 64-bit Linux host that fits the system requirements; installation is via a provided installer script
Installation and authoring details are in external documentation rather than the README
